Class Violation

java.lang.Object
iu.validation.Violation
All Implemented Interfaces:
IuConstraintViolation
final class Violation extends Object implements IuConstraintViolation
One constraint failure.

Attributes and the interpolated message are resolved eagerly. A violation is only ever created for a value that actually failed, so this reflection is paid on the error path rather than on every validated property.

  • Method Details

    • path

      public String path()
      Description copied from interface: IuConstraintViolation
      Gets the rendered path from the validated root object to the invalid value, for example details[2].strm or byCode[ABCD]<key>.

      Always names at least one property: every constraint this module evaluates is declared on a property, so nothing fails at the root object itself. See IuValidationNodeKind for the rendering rule of each segment.

      Specified by:
      path in interface IuConstraintViolation
      Returns:
      dotted and bracketed property path; never null, never empty

    • attributes

      public Map<String,Object> attributes()
      Description copied from interface: IuConstraintViolation
      Gets the declared attributes of the constraint annotation, for example regexp and flags for Pattern.

      Includes message, groups, and payload. These are the values a JSON Schema or OpenAPI generator needs in order to translate the constraint into a schema keyword.

      Specified by:
      attributes in interface IuConstraintViolation
      Returns:
      unmodifiable attribute map keyed by annotation method name; never null

    • invalidValue

      public Object invalidValue()
      Description copied from interface: IuConstraintViolation
      Gets the value that failed the constraint.

      Excluded from IuConstraintViolation.describe() and from IuValidationResult.report() because validated input is frequently sensitive. Use IuValidationResult.report(boolean) to opt a rendered report into including values.

      Specified by:
      invalidValue in interface IuConstraintViolation
      Returns:
      invalid value; may be null, since NotNull is failed by a null value
